messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: Real-time alert: eu-west-2 streaming-gateway p99 tail latency breach detected at 2026-03-15T02:12:03Z. metric: stream_tail_p99=3.2s (SLO=1.5s). Paging oncall.

Jules: ack — I'm awake. pulling up grafana and traces. which AZs/pods look worst?

Alex: eu-west-2a proxies show sustained TLS handshake retries and elevated tcp_retransmit. Also seeing spike in ephemeral_port_in_use on nat-gw-a (~96%). conntrack entries high on proxy hosts.

NetOps: Confirmed NAT utilisation: nat-gw-a=96%, nat-gw-b=67%, conntrack on proxy-fleet nearing 90% of max in 2 hosts. DNS forwarder in azc hitting high CPU from a bunch of cross-zone queries.

Jules: customer impact: several streaming sessions stall for multiple seconds; some clients drop and reconnect resulting in churn. p95 has jumped to ~480ms. We need an immediate mitigation window to protect SLOs.

Sara: quick runbook plan (short list):
- shift egress for streaming-gateway away from nat-gw-a to nat-gw-b
- scale streaming-proxy ASG +4 instances
- temporarily bump conntrack max and run an expedited GC pass
- add local DNS cache on proxies to reduce forwarder load

Mike: Initiating NAT rebind now. Request to attach ephemeral pool on nat-gw-b submitted -> AWS returned accept, applying route/target updates.

Alex: snippets from proxy logs around 02:11:
```
[02:11:58] tls: handshake timeout id=0x3f2a remote=10.4.22.9:443 attempts=4
[02:12:01] stream: stall duration=1700ms session=abc123
```

NetOps: I'm also seeing DNS SERVFAIL bursts for internal resolver when cross-AZ queries spike. Adding a ttl=30 cache on proxies to reduce resolver pressure.

Jules: Exec plan: 1) steer new sessions to nat-gw-b (Mike), 2) scale ASG +4 (Sara), 3) apply conntrack GC / sysctls on proxies (Alex). Monitor 5m.

Mike: Route changes propagated at 02:14:40Z -> traffic shift observed for new flows. ephemeral usage on nat-gw-a dropped to 72% within 90s.

Sara: ASG scale executed, 4 new proxy instances booting -> healthchecks passing around 02:16:10Z.

Alex: applied expedited conntrack GC & sysctl patch on one rolling shard:
```
echo 2 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# trigger manual GC
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_acct
```

Jules: telemetry update: p99 improved from 3.2s -> 1.3s half-life, p95 ~300ms. Streaming stalls alerts reduced by ~75%. Still watching for DNS anomalies.

NetOps: Found stray /32 route to an old proxy ASG causing some sessions to still egress via nat-gw-a -> cleaning route now.

customer-ops-bot: Drafting customer advisory for affected customers (top-10). Posting to #customer-notifications for review. Will send initial notice within 30m.

Mike: New proxies in service, 4/4 healthy at 02:16:20Z. Traffic rebalanced.

Alex: running short tcpdump to verify handshake success rate now:
```
tcpdump -nn -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0' -c 100
```

Jules: metrics snapshot 02:18Z: p95=310ms, p99=890ms, tcp_retransmit back to baseline, dns_errors down.

NetOps: preliminary root-cause hypothesis: a small release yesterday increased short-lived connection churn, together with uneven ephemeral port allocation on nat-gw-a and a heated DNS forwarder in azc. Cascade: more retries -> more conntrack entries -> more NAT ports consumed -> handshake timeouts -> stalls.

Sara: post-incident actions:
- add automated ephemeral pool auto-scale and health-based failover (NetOps)
- deploy local DNS cache layer on proxy AMI (eng-runtime)
- tune default conntrack limits and GC frequency in infra images (eng-infra)
- implement early synthetic cross-AZ streaming probe to catch handshake regressions (eng-sre)

Jules: I'm handing off to Alex for followup and write-up. I'll be off pager at 02:30Z. Alex take point.

Alex: ack. I'll keep the channel open until 02:45Z, prepare initial incident doc, and open a postmortem ticket. Escalate to infra-if p99 > 1.5s.

incident_bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial. Pager cleared. Incident ID: INC-20260315-5554321987.

customer-ops-bot: Customer notification scheduled at 02:25Z. Follow-up update in 60m with remediation summary.

Alex: 02:27Z status: p99 stable ~880ms, no new pages. Closing immediate paging but oncall watch for another 30m.

Jules: thanks team :thumbsup: — special thanks to Mike and NetOps for fast NAT failover.

NetOps: I'll run a replay of the spike against staging NAT topology tomorrow and validate automated failover playbook.

Alex: Handoff complete. tagging @postmortem. Good coordination everyone.
